method.response_alignment: journal dispatch/completion paired by request_id and order; response content exactly equals all_responses and step agent_response
method.tool_alignment: ordered official tool_results paired with observer operations only for step/get_available_actions/end_game
method.feedback_alignment: next request preserves preceding message prefix and appends exact prior assistant response plus official error or exact trajectory tool result
method.relative_monotonic_origin: first request dispatch in each trajectory; zero is not episode start
method.score_time_window: score-changing operation occurs after that response completion and before next request dispatch; last step uses later batch_close as conservative upper bound
method.observer_timestamp_limitation: operation records contain duration but no absolute start/end; windows are brackets, not exact score timestamps
method.http_duration: end_monotonic_s minus start_monotonic_s; excludes dispatch validation/reservation and is not pure model generation latency
method.wall_duration: saved perf_counter duration around evaluator plus environment observer cleanup; excludes earlier setup and later HTTP/client cleanup
method.official_time: recorded official logical time, including virtual tool duration and noisy system time; never substituted for wall duration
method.score_at_unobserved_steps: null; no synthetic per-step score snapshot added
method.no_content_repair: malformed model output remains unchanged; only official parser replayed offline

answerable_mechanisms: Whether an unparseable reply is followed by the official error observation in the next serialized request.
Whether the next observed reply becomes parseable and executes a tool; this is observed protocol recovery, not a feedback treatment effect.
Which observed tool steps change raw score and whether recovery itself changes score.
Recorded transport time, between-request gaps, and broad monotonic score-transition windows within each individual trajectory.
not_identified: Whether error feedback caused recovery rather than resampling, accumulated context, model behavior, or provider behavior.
Whether v2 caused fewer format failures, or whether one model is better/faster under a common deadline: these are three unmatched trajectories with different prompts, limits and virtual delays.
Counterfactual score gains from repairing sooner, suppressing feedback, or continuing with another model.
Statistical repair rates, significance, task-general mechanisms, held-out prefix prediction, or latency-generalizing crossover.
Exact real-time score-change instants, pure model compute latency, or service-side causes of malformed content.

minimal_missing_fields_for_future_runs.purpose: same-origin episode timeline and exact wall-clock deadline accounting
direct tool/score alignment rather than ordered matching and time brackets
explicit decision-time feedback provenance without re-reading text
deadline winner requires an available selected result, not completed-response count
identify matched interventions and held-out prediction; fields alone cannot substitute for additional experimental cells
